hints.content:
The x-coordinates of the points where the graphs of the equations $y=f(x)$ and $y=g(x)$ intersect are the solutions of the equation $f(x)=g(x)$.

In our case, $f(x)=2x^2+3x-2$ and $g(x)=-4$. We already have $f$ graphed, and the graph of $g$ is a horizontal line. Let's add it and see what we get.

[[☃ image 1]]

Both $f$ and $g$ are now graphed, and every point where they intersect represents a solution of $f(x)=g(x)$.

options.alt: A parabola and a horizontal line on an x y coordinate plane. The x- and y- axes scale by one. The graph has a vertex around (negative one, negative three). It is concave up decreasing from the interval of negative infinity to around negative one passing through the point (negative two, zero) and increases from the interval around negative one to infinity passing through the point (one, three). The horizontal line is at y equals negative four.

hints.content: The graphs don't intersect, so the equation has *no solutions*.
